deep.reconstruction:
PURPOSE. The page reduces meridian zenith distances of γ Ursae Majoris, observed at lower culmination at Göttingen from 27 Oct to 28 Nov 1818, to mean place. It then derives the latitude of the observatory. The previous page does the same reduction for another star; the next page does it for 'Anonyma 1'. Angles written like 213.51 mean 213°51′, not decimals.

A. Reduction to mean place at 10-day steps (Oct 27, Nov 6, 16, 26, Dec 6). Four terms are computed for RA (in seconds of time) and for Dec (in arcseconds).

(1) Precession.
- t is the time from 1819.0, in days: −64.599, −54.628, −44.656, −34.685, −24.713. The steps of 9.971–9.972 days are the interval between successive culminations, 10 × (1 − 1/366.25).
- log|t| = 1.81022n, 1.73741n, … ('n' marks a negative number).
- RA term = t·10^(7.94223−10) s/day = 0.0087535 t. Annually this is (m + n sinα tanδ)/15 ≈ 3.197 s.
- Dec term = t·10^(8.73836−10)n = −0.054747 t ″/day, i.e. n cosα ≈ −20.00″/yr.
- Result: RA row −0.5655 … −0.2163; Dec row +3.537 … (+1.353 on Dec 6).

(2) Annual aberration.
- ⊙ is the Sun's longitude: 213°51′, 223°51′, 233°53′, 243°58′, 254°06′.
- RA term = 10^0.33889 · sin(⊙ + 94°18′) = 2.1823 sin(⊙ + 94°18′) s.
- Dec term = 10^1.23502 · sin(⊙ + 347°38′) = 17.180 sin(⊙ + 347°38′)″. The angle 347.38 at the foot of the column is this declination phase.
- These are the standard expressions −κ secδ(cosα cosε cos⊙ + sinα sin⊙) and the corresponding Dec formula, rewritten in amplitude-phase form.
- With δ ≈ 54°42′ and α ≈ 176°04′, my check of the phase (−12°22′) matches exactly.
- Both amplitudes imply κ ≈ 20.6″ (my inference).

(3) Lunar nutation.
- Ω is the longitude of the Moon's node: 29°15′, 28°43′, 28°12′, 27°40′, 27°09′.
- RA term = 10^0.13233 · sin(Ω + 141°45′) = 1.3563 sin(Ω + 141°45′) s.
- Dec term = 10^0.82390 · sin(Ω + 5°17′) = 6.664 sin(Ω + 5°17′)″. The angle 5.17 at the foot of the column is this declination phase.
- Decomposing gives roughly Ψ ≈ 16.7″ in longitude and N ≈ 8.96″ in obliquity (my inference). That is close to the Lindenau/Bessel constant 8.977″.

(4) Solar (semiannual) nutation.
- Argument 2⊙: 67°42′, 87°42′, 107°46′, 127°56′, 148°12′.
- RA term = 10^(8.87884−10) · sin(2⊙ + 147°24′) = 0.07564 sin(2⊙ + 147°24′) s.
- Dec term = 10^(9.60025−10) · sin(2⊙ + 4°18′) = 0.3984 sin(2⊙ + 4°18′)″.

Sums of the four terms:
- RA: −2.1129, −1.7725, −1.3777, −0.9378, −0.4622 s.
- Dec: +1.403, −1.855, −4.896, −7.644, −10.019″. The Dec 6 value comes from the separately written column 1.353 − 15.131 + 3.575 + 0.184.

B. A 5-day table (Oct 27 … Dec 6) is formed by halving with second differences: midpoint = (a + b)/2 − Δ²/8.
- Example: Nov 1 Dec = (1.403 − 1.855)/2 − 0.217/8 = −0.253 ≈ −0.25.
- Example: Nov 1 RA = −1.9427 − 0.0068 = −1.95.

C. Linear interpolation to the observation dates gives the Dec corrections:
- Nov 3: −0.89; Nov 4: −1.21; Nov 5: −1.53; Nov 10: −3.10.
- Nov 12: −3.71; Nov 13: −4.01; Nov 15: −4.60; Nov 25: −7.37; Nov 28: −8.14.

D. Each correction is added to the observed zenith distance. At lower culmination z = 180° − φ − δ, so z_reduced = z_apparent + Δδ.
- Series I (Oct 27 – Nov 10, about 73°38′17″) has mean 73°38′17.04″.
- Series II (Nov 11 – 28, about 73°53′52″) has mean 73°53′51.92″.
- The difference is 15′34.88″, written at the foot of the page. The previous page shows a similar jump (15′40.24″) for its star at the same date.
- I read this as two instrument positions with index error ±7′47″, eliminated by taking the mean (my interpretation): z = (73°38′17.04″ + 73°53′51.92″)/2 = 73°46′4.48″.

E. Latitude. Using the mean polar distance p = 90° − δ = 35°17′55.30″ (δ = 54°42′4.70″ for 1819.0):
- φ = p + 90° − z = 35°17′55.30″ + 90° − 73°46′4.48″ = 51°31′50.82″.
- This is the latitude of the Göttingen observatory; the accepted value is about 51°31′48″.
- Refraction must already have been applied to the listed z, since the result is correct to a few arcseconds (my inference).
errors: Nov 5: 17.86 − 1.53 = 16.33. The value reads 16.35 in the transcription and is ambiguous in the image. Either way the series mean of 17.04 is unaffected.
5-day RA table, Dec 1: halving with second differences gives about −0.704 (−0.70), but −0.71 is written. This is a 0.01 s discrepancy, and the RA column is not used in the latitude computation.
Implicit step, not an error: refraction is not applied on this page, so the zenith distances must already be refraction-corrected. Otherwise the latitude would be off by about 3′.
No other arithmetic errors were found. All logs, products, sums, interpolations, means and the final latitude check.

results.what: Reduction of a star from mean place (1819.0) to apparent place: precession, annual aberration, lunar and solar nutation in amplitude-phase form A·sin(arg + phase)
results.modern_name: Apparent-place reduction (precursor of Bessel day numbers / independent star numbers)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard practice (Bradley, Delambre, Zach tables); systematized by Bessel (Tabulae Regiomontanae, 1830)

results.what: Interpolation of halfway values using second differences (subtract Δ²/8)
Latitude from lower-culmination zenith distances: φ = 90° − z + p, with the index error eliminated by averaging two instrument positions
results.modern_name: Latitude determination by meridian zenith distances of circumpolar stars

results.what: Latitude of the Göttingen observatory found as 51°31′50.82″ from γ UMa, 1818

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine observatory reduction work: precession, aberration and nutation, then latitude from culminations. Gauss's Göttingen latitude work is well known. The only mildly interesting detail is the implied constants: aberration ≈ 20.6″ and nutation ≈ 9.0″, which could document which tables Gauss used in 1818.

transcription_corrections: Angles are degrees.minutes: '254.6' = 254°06′, '27.9' = 27°09′, '244.0'-type entries = 244°00′. They are not decimals.

'347.38' under the aberration columns is the declination aberration phase 347°38′. '5.17' and '4.18' are the declination phases for lunar and solar nutation. '8.73836n' is log(n cosα) per day for declination precession.
Nov 5 reduced value: arithmetic gives 16.33; the image is ambiguous between 16.33 and 16.35.
The last value in the right-hand column is clearly '51.31.50.82' (latitude); no [?] is needed. '15 34.88' at the bottom is the difference 15′34.88″ between the two series means.
'Oct 27 −2"11' should read −2.11 (seconds of time, RA correction).
